Alex / Priya / team —

Thanks for the clear targets. Below is a technical recap and initial recommendations based on the numbers you shared and our typical patterns. I attached a simple architecture diagram and an SLO metrics workbook for reference (architecture-diagram.png, redwood-slo-metrics.xlsx).

Summary of constraints and assumptions:
- Typical request: ~75 tokens in + ~40 tokens out => ~115 tokens total.
- p95 latency target: <= 250ms (short prompt distribution).
- Peak sustained throughput: 300 QPS.
- Model candidates: Llama2-13B / Mistral-7B / Falcon-40B (tradeoffs noted below).

Latency & throughput notes:
- For p95 <= 250ms at 300 QPS, we recommend Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) with autoscaling buffer. Hosted burst can work for prototyping but cost & tail latency variability increase.
- Continuous batching: target small inter-batch delay (~5-10ms) and max batch sizes tuned by sequence-length distribution. This typically gives best unit cost while keeping tail latency bounded.
- KV cache: for retrieval-augmented workflows, prefix caching reduces computation for repeated contexts; ensure cache placement is local to the serving shard to avoid network hop penalties.
- Quantization: FP16 or 4-bit quantization for larger models (Falcon-40B) can significantly reduce latency per token and GPU memory footprint; expect ~20-40% improvement depending on kernel-level support.

Sizing guidance (ballpark):
- Llama2-13B (quantized): ~6-8 GPUs (A10 / H100 equivalent) to sustain 300 QPS with target p95 if aggressively batched and with KV caching.
- Mistral-7B: ~3-4 GPUs for same workload; better p95 at lower cost but with tradeoffs on output quality for some prompt types.
- Falcon-40B (quantized): 4-6 H100-equivalent GPUs if using high compute kernels; expect improved single-request latencies but higher memory and orchestration complexity.

Multi-region & failover:
- Active-active multi-region recommended for strict availability — route traffic by latency policy with automatic failover to secondary region.
- Keep model variants pinned and replicate model artifacts to regional stores; startup time for large models can be non-trivial (minutes) unless you maintain warm pools.

Operational recommendations:
- Canary & A/B: run small percentage traffic to new model variant for quality + perf checks.
- Tracing: instrument per-request token latency and batch queue wait times; surface p95/p99 per-route in Redwood Console dashboards.
- Cost controls: configure burst caps and soft limits per-route to avoid cost spikes during unexpected traffic.

Open questions / info needed from Acme:
- Representative token histogram / qps per minute across peak window
- Expected concurrency distribution (bursty vs steady)
- Any hard constraints on model families or licensing (open vs commercial)

Action items (we'll own the first two):
- Marcus: prepare a sizing + topology note (attached) and a short runbook for PoC (estimated 2-3 week timeline).
- Marissa: coordinate calendar and procurement touchpoints.
- Acme: share telemetry and availability windows for the PoC.

Attachments:

- redwood-slo-metrics.xlsx (SLO calc, GPU estimates, cost ranges)
